phenotypicFeatures.description: dysexecutive syndrome (affective instability, sensory overload, concentration, and impulse control problems)
continuous headache
cognitive deficits (memory difficulties and needing more time to learn than her siblings)
repeated syncopations
hyperpigmentation
early morning nausea
no appetite and could eat very little
Addison crisis with hypotension, diarrhea/vomiting, hypoglycemia, vigilance reduction, and metabolic acidosis
self-limiting, discrete hemiparesis on the right side
two grand mal seizures
progressive disorientation, reduced vigilance, headache, coordination disturbances and, again, hemiparesis on the right side
subacute left parieto-occipital cortical/subcortical lesion involving the precentral gyrus with T2-weighted FLAIR signal increase and diffusion restriction without respecting vascular territories

intermittent slowing temporoparietal on both sides (stronger on the left) and singular spike-wave complexes temporal (once temporoparietal) on the left

Addison's disease
normochromic, normocytic anemia
mild to moderate antrum gastritis suspicious of chronic toxic (type C) gastritis
more than three-fold increase in lactate levels compared to resting state values
single cytochrome c oxidase (COX)-negative muscle fibers

increased anti-thyroglobulin, increased anti-thyroid peroxidase, anti-adrenal cortex, anti-glutamic acid decarboxylase (GAD-65), anti-partial cell, anti-intrinsic factor, and anti-nuclear antibodies (ANAs)
